subject: Urgent: VaultPay live ingest errors & p99 latency — exec escalations
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@vaultpay.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@vaultpay.com>, QA Team <qa@vaultpay.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: VaultPay live ingest — sudden spike in 500s and p99 latency

Team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in error rates across our live ingest pipeline at ~08:50 EDT — p50 latency is fine but p99 has spiked to ~18s and error rate (5xx) jumped from 0.3% to 6.8% in ~20 minutes. This is impacting card settlement jobs and a few merchants have reported timeouts.

Quick facts:
- Region: us-east-1
- Client SDK version: 1.8.4 (rolled out this morning)
- Sample trace_ids: vp-20260815-1932, vp-20260815-1947 (attached)

Attached: error-samples.log (snips), live-ingest-metrics-20260815.csv

We need an immediate remediation plan — our ops and product teams are on a call. Can you please triage urgently? If this is on Redwood's side we need a rollback path or mitigation ASAP.

Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Integrations, VaultPay
[Attachment: error-samples.log (text/plain)]
[Attachment: live-ingest-metrics-20260815.csv (text/csv)]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@vaultpay.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VaultPay live ingest — sudden spike in 500s and p99 latency

Samir — thanks for the quick heads up and for the attachments. I'm very sorry for the disruption. We're opening an incident and pulling the integration team now.

Initial ask: can you confirm whether you have HTTP-level traces showing split/chunked header frames around those trace_ids (I see several 502/500s referencing "malformed headers")? If you can paste a single raw request/response (redact PII) that will speed up triage.

CC'ing Naomi (Solutions) and Sean (SRE) for immediate log pulls. Vanessa, can your team review client SDK 1.8.4 release notes and surface any streaming/header changes? If we need a rollback path we should decide in the next 20–30m.

I will escalate to execs if needed but want a quick technical mitigation first.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

> On Sat, Aug 15, 2026 at 09:14 AM Samir Khan <samir@vaultpay.com> wrote:
> > Team,
> > We started seeing a sharp increase in error rates ...

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, samir@vaultpay.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VaultPay live ingest — sudden spike in 500s and p99 latency

Hi all — quick update from integration log analysis.

What we see: several inbound streaming requests from VaultPay's SDK exhibit header fragmentation where the client sends header bytes across multiple frames without the expected continuation markers; our streaming parser (server-side HTTP/2/WS adapter) treats the second chunk as payload in a small number of cases, which results in a malformed header block and the upstream runtime returning a 500.

Evidence: I attached a screenshot snippet from the proxy trace showing the header boundary split and an extracted request sample with the trace_id vp-20260815-1947. The pattern started immediately after your SDK rollout to 1.8.4.

Immediate suggestions:
- If VaultPay can pin clients back to SDK 1.8.3 we will see immediate error-rate improvement.
- On our side, we can push a tolerant parser patch to the ingress layer to tolerate split header frames for the next 24 hours while we release a server-side fix. That patch is low-risk and can be canaried.

Next steps: Vanessa/Sean, can you confirm the ETA for the ingress patch? Samir, can your QA kick off a rollback to 1.8.3 for a subset of traffic while we deploy?

Naomi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: screenshot-500.png (image/png)]

From: Samir Khan <samir@vaultpay.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@vaultpay.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 10:21:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VaultPay live ingest — sudden spike in 500s and p99 latency

Rishi / Naomi,

Thanks — we can rollback to 1.8.3 but that will take ~2 hours to coordinate across our fleet (canary -> full). This issue is already causing settlements to queue; Elena (VP Ops) is joining this thread. At a minimum we expect a temporary credits discussion if this continues beyond today — we have committed merchants seeing delayed settlements which has direct revenue impact.

I'll start the rollback now and report status in 30m. Please prioritize the ingress patch canary.

Samir

> On Sat, Aug 15, 2026 at 10:05 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Hi all — quick update from integration log analysis...

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, samir@vaultpay.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VaultPay live ingest — sudden spike in 500s and p99 latency

On it. Quick mitigation plan (can be executed in next 45m):

1) Canary deploy ingress tolerant-parser patch to us-east-1 (5% of traffic) — ETA 25m. Patch will relax strict header-continuation checks and coalesce split frames into a single header block.
2) Temporary routing rule: route VaultPay traffic through a small proxy pool that applies a defensive reassembly fallback for header fragments — ETA 45m.
3) Coordinate VaultPay rollback to SDK 1.8.3 for canary merchants (Samir to confirm subset).

I'll own rollout and will post back with canary metrics. If canary stabilizes error-rate <0.5% and p99 <3s, we hold and then schedule a permanent runtime fix in the next release.

Action items:
- Samir: confirm rollback subset and provide any remaining trace samples.
- Sean: prepare rollback playbook and incident postmortem template.
- Jonas: please standby for a short exec brief if we need credits/comp escalation.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Integrations Engineering, Redwood Inference

[Related ops doc: https://redwood-internal/ops/incidents/INC-20260815-VP]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@vaultpay.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@vaultpay.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 18:02:00 -0400
Subject: VaultPay incident — exec summary, credits, and next steps

Samir / Elena — thanks to everyone for the rapid coordination. Quick executive summary and ask:

Summary:
- Root cause: client-side header fragmentation introduced in VaultPay SDK 1.8.4 interacting with our streaming parser, producing malformed header blocks and triggering server 5xxs.
- Immediate mitigation: VaultPay rollback to SDK 1.8.3 (canary -> fleet) + Redwood ingress tolerant-parser canary. Both measures reduced 5xx to ~0.4% and p99 back to ~2.6s within the canary window.
- Timeline: canary rollback + ingress patch completed on 2026-08-15 between 11:00–12:00 EDT; full rollback completed by 14:00 EDT. Permanent runtime fix scheduled for 2026-08-20 release.

Executive asks:
1) Credits: We propose a goodwill credit for affected settlements on Aug 15 (we will work with Finance to size this and get you a proposal by EOD Monday).
2) Postmortem: Redwood will provide a joint postmortem and coordinated release notes for SDK 1.8.4 highlighting the fragmentation edge-case and recommended client-side guardrails.
3) SLA/contract: Jonas (copied) will review whether this incident meets thresholds for an SLA exception; we will route as needed.

I appreciate your patience and will follow up with the postmortem and credit proposal. If VaultPay needs an emergency support arrangement we can escalate to an interim dedicated capacity window.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
